In April 2021, Wisk sued Archer for“brazen theft” of confidential information and intellectual property. The legal wrangling lasted two years before the companies reached an unusual settlement that not only ended the lawsuit as well as Archer’s counter-suit against Wisk seeking $1 billion in damages, but kicked off a new collaboration. Under the terms of the settlement, Archer agreed to make Wisk the exclusive provider of autonomous technology. Archer also agreed, at the time, to give Wisk the option to purchase up to 13,176,636 shares of common stock at a price of $0.01 per share.

On August 9, 2026, Archer Aviation Inc. (the “Company”) entered into a definitive Equity Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) with The Boeing Company (“Boeing”) to acquire all of the equity interests of Wisk Aero LLC, an autonomous aviation company, SkyGrid, LLC, a digital airspace integration and air traffic management platform, and Insitu, Inc., a manufacturer of unmanned aircraft systems and AI-enabled technologies, together with certain of their respective related entities, including Insitu Pacific Pty Ltd, Wisk Australia Pty Ltd, and Boeing Emirates Ltd (collectively, the “Target Companies”, and such acquisition, the “Acquisition”).

highlights:
Archer to acquire Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu from Boeing - FlightGlobal

# Archer to acquire Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu from Boeing
...
Included with Archer's acquisition of Boeing subsidiaries will be eVTOL developer Wisk, which is developing an autonomous electric air taxi that was until now seen as a rival to Archer's Midnight eVTOL Wisk Aero
...
Advanced air mobility start-up Archer Aviation has reached a deal to acquire several emerging aerospace technology companies owned by Boeing.
...
The agreement covers electric aircraft developer Wisk, uncrewed aerial systems manufacturer Insitu and air traffic management solutions provider SkyGrid. Although the specific terms have not been disclosed, Archer says it has “signed definitive agreements” with Boeing covering the acquisitions.
...
An 8-K filing with US securities regulators on 9 August reveals that Boeing will take a nearly 20% ownership stake in Archer via stock transfer in exchange for the three companies. Additionally, Boeing will be granted warrants allowing it to purchase $200 million in Archer stock over the next several years at a fixed price.
